title: New Mexico methods, restrictions, and GMU rules

methods.label: Bow
methods.summary: Longbow, recurve, or compound bow meeting NMDGF draw-weight and broadhead rules. Crossbows are a separate sporting-arm class where listed.

methods.label: Muzzleloader
methods.summary: Muzzleloading rifles meeting caliber and ignition rules for the hunt code. Scopes and sabots follow the current booklet.

methods.label: Any legal firearm / rifle
methods.summary: Centerfire rifles and other legal firearms listed for the hunt code. Magazine and caliber restrictions apply.

methods.label: Any legal sporting arm
methods.summary: Any sporting arm legal for that species under NMDGF rules for the hunt code.

methods.label: Shotgun
methods.summary: Shotguns for turkey, dove, and small game as listed; non-toxic shot where required for waterfowl.

prohibited: Hunting without the license and carcass tag (or e-tag) required for that species.
Hunting public land with a private-land-only license.
Using bait for big game where prohibited in the current rules.
Shooting from or across a public road.
Hunting in closed areas, national parks, or tribal land without tribal authorization.
unitRules: A hunt code is legal only in the GMUs printed for that code in the Hunting Rules & Info.
WMA-only hunts are restricted to the named wildlife management area inside the GMU.
Weapon type (bow, muzzleloader, any legal firearm) is part of the hunt code — do not assume any-weapon.
Bag limits and antler restrictions are per hunt code; one deer or elk license per hunter per year in most cases.
